An Iranian film director, screenwriter, poet and photographer from Tehran, the best known figure of the Iranian New Wave in cinema.

He started in graphic design and advertising. In 1969 he set up a film section at a state institute for children's education, where he made short films for and about children for many years. He stayed in Iran after the Iranian Revolution of 1979, when many artists left, and kept working inside its censorship.

His films mix fiction and documentary and use amateur actors, long takes and car journeys on country roads. They include:

  • Where Is the Friend's House? (1987), the first of a trilogy set around the village of Koker;
  • Close-Up (1990), about a real man who pretended to be a famous director;
  • Taste of Cherry (1997), which won the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival;
  • The Wind Will Carry Us (1999);
  • Certified Copy (2010), made in Italy.

He brought world attention to Iranian cinema and helped younger directors, writing scripts for Jafar Panahi. He died in Paris in 2016.
sum: An Iranian film director, screenwriter, poet and photographer from Tehran, the best known figure of the Iranian New Wave in cinema.
